title: ops-sync-scratchpad: sre weekly prep & reliability review
content:
Purpose: prep notes for SRE ops sync (weekly) + reliability review. Informal scratchpad — bring the numbers, raise blockers, agree action items.

Meeting: SRE Weekly Ops Sync — Thu 10:00-11:00 PT (recurring)
Attendees: oncall, infra, serving-runtime leads, release-eng rep, product-ops (optional)

Agenda draft (topline):
- Quick wins / rollups (5m)
- Paging trends & oncall load (10m)
- SLO status and error-budget burn (15m)
- Top incidents since last sync (20m)
- Immediate mitigations + runbook gaps (5m)
- Action items and owners (5m)

Notes / data to pull before meeting (TODO):
- Error budget: service-alpha (web-gen) 7-day burn = 3.8% (target 1%/7d) => flag.
- P99 latency for text-generation (hosted-api) = 420ms (baseline target 200ms p99).
- Paging: average pages/day last 7d = 9.2 (oncall load spike on Mon 3/9: 28 pages).
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) last week = 4m, mean time to resolve (MTTR) = 47m.
- Incidents: 3 Sev2-ish (cache-thrash, autoscaler misconfig, datastore throttling).
- Pull dashboards: /dashboards/slo-overview, /dashboards/paging-trends (link in linked_artifacts).

Paging trends quick analysis (notes to self):
- Spike correlated with canary rollout for model v2.1 (deployment cluster us-west-2-d).
- Root cause shorthand: unexpected KV cache eviction due to memory pressure after unbounded prefix caching.
- Oncall signal: 60% of pages were for elevated 5xx from serving-runtime.
- Actionable question: was the canary pinned to small batch sizes? check rollout config (release-eng).

Top incidents (short summaries):
1) Incident: cache-thrashing during model-v2.1 canary (2026-03-09 02:14 UTC)
   - Symptom: P50->P99 latency spike and elevated 5xxs for ~45m during canary ramp.
   - Root cause: aggressive prefix caching + insufficient eviction heuristic -> OOMs on some GPU hosts -> fallback path overloaded.
   - Mitigation taken: rolled back canary to v2.0, scaled up cache memory on affected pool, temporary throttling rule added for new canaries.
   - Open: add pre-deployment cache-pressure check to CI, instrument eviction counts in canary alerts.

2) Incident: autoscaler misconfiguration for dedicated pool (2026-03-10 11:05 UTC)
   - Symptom: queue backlog for dedicated-reserved -> increased latency, partial request drops.
   - Root cause: HPA target incorrectly set to cpu% instead of traffic-based metric.
   - Mitigation: manual hotspot scaling + config patch to use request-per-second metric.
   - Open: write automated test for autoscaler config; rollback policy clarity for Dedicated.

3) Incident: datastore throttling in eu-central (2026-03-11 18:30 UTC)
   - Symptom: slow metadata reads -> request retries -> higher token cost and slightly increased latencies.
   - Note: affected only internal batch jobs during redeploy window.
   - Mitigation: added retry backoff + moved heavy jobs to maintenance window.
   - Open: investigate metadata caching TTLs and multi-region read fallbacks.

SLOs snapshot (to present):
- Hosted API availability (global) SLO: 99.95% monthly. Last 30d = 99.92% -> 0.03% breach risk if current trend continues.
- Generation correctness SLO (sampled evals): pass rate 97.6% (target 98.5%) -> regression candidate.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 220ms (current p95 = 266ms), p99 < 500ms (current p99 = 420ms).

Immediate mitigations to propose in meeting:
- Temp tighten canary ramp for model submissions (max 10% traffic until perf telemetry passes 30m). Owner: Arjun Rao. Due: 2026-03-14
- Add eviction count metric & alert (critical for memory pressure). Owner: Lina García. Due: 2026-03-16
- Autoscaler config test + enforce traffic metric default. Owner: Priya Shah (release-eng). Due: 2026-03-20
- Short-term routing fallback for eu reads to cross-region (soft-fail) for metadata reads. Owner: Jamie Thompson. Due: 2026-03-17

Runbook / playbook gaps noticed (notes):
- No clear 'canary memory pressure' runbook. Create: checklist of signals (eviction rate, OOM count, queue backlog) + emergency rollback steps.
- Pager fatigue: many low-signal pages for transient spikes. Idea: add severity filter or implement paging threshold for noisy alerts.

Data asks for meeting (assign to metrics owner):
- SLO burn rate per service for last 14 days, with annotations for deploys.
- Pages by type (5xx, throttling, latency, infra) for last 7 days and per-oncall.
- Correlate deploys with p99 latency changes (per region).

Questions to raise / discuss:
- Do we keep current error budget policy for beta customers during rapid model iteration? (risk vs velocity tradeoff)
- Can Dedicated customers opt-out of aggressive prefix caching? (privacy/perf config flag)
- Are we comfortable with current cooldowns on autoscaler or should we make them more conservative?

Follow-ups (personal action list):
- Prep a 2-slide summary for Thursday: 1) SLO / pages headline, 2) proposed mitigations + action owners. (Jamie) Due: 2026-03-13 morning.
- Draft the 'canary memory pressure' runbook skeleton and share in #sre-runbooks. (Jamie) Due: 2026-03-16.
- Ping product-ops re: correctness SLO regression (sample set + evaluation harness). (Jamie -> Product) Due: 2026-03-15.

Notes to self (informal):
- Flagging model v2.1 rollout as high-risk until eviction metrics present.
- Consider adding a short-lived 'no-caching' toggle for canaries to reduce footprint. Easy to add via runtime flags?
- Check whether the hosted-api p99 regression aligns with quantization change in v2.1.

- Jira: autoscaler ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-1024

- GitHub PR for rollback logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/612

Status: draft scratchpad — will clean up into meeting slides and agenda doc after validating metrics.

End of scratchpad.
